purpose: Licensed intentional divergences across the SDK/CLI/MCP surfaces: schema kinds (extra-param, widened-type, name-for-id, omitted-param) plus the cross-surface behavior kind. Every divergence a checker can observe must carry a license entry here; an unlicensed divergence reds, and a license entry with no matching divergence in the code (rot) reds too, in both directions. This file was created ahead of its checker (P6); scripts/check-mcp-schema-parity.mjs landed with W2 in two halves: W2a licensed the widened-type coercion family and emitted the parameter-level schema artifact; W2b (this batch) adds the full per-operation extra-param diff -- the naive resolution strategy the original card asked for (guessing a request-body file name from operationId) was fragile, so the checker instead calls scripts/sdk-codegen/model.mjs's buildModel(doc) (the real generator's own resolver, imported read-only, never edited) to get the exact SDK-side path/query/body param set per operation, camelCased with the same toCamel the generator uses, and diffs it against docs/mcp-tool-schemas.json's inputSchema.properties (minus the universal dry_run/confirm_token write-confirmation params, already licensed above under the risky-write-tools behavior entry). extra-param entries below carry operationIds + extraParams so the checker can verify both directions structurally, not by parsing prose. omitted-param stays informational per the card's own scopeStop -- an MCP tool exposing fewer filters than the raw operation is not a divergence needing a license, and is not checked here.

entries.operationOrFamily: every MCP tool parameter built with zStringList(...) or zNumberLike(...)
entries.reason: mcp/src/arg-shapes.ts's zStringList/zNumberLike wrap a field in z.preprocess so the server also accepts a bare string where the wire type is an array ("x" => ["x"]) or a numeric string where the wire type is a number ("40.5" => 40.5) -- forgiving model-emitted arguments. This is a single family license, not one entry per call site (205 call sites across mcp/src/tools/**/*.ts at licensing time, dominated by the page/pageSize pagination pair on nearly every list tool): the MCP SDK's zod-to-json-schema conversion unwraps z.preprocess to the INNER schema, so the model-visible tool schema in docs/mcp-tool-schemas.json already reports the canonical array/number type -- only the server's runtime acceptance widens, and it widens identically everywhere the two helpers are used.

The CLI's delete command for an active project or client archives it first, then deletes, via wrapper/ensure.ts's archiveThenDelete core (archiveThenDeleteProject / archiveThenDeleteClient) -- the Clockify API rejects deleting an active project or client directly. SDK and MCP callers building on the raw API surface do not get this chain automatically; only the CLI's delete command wires it in. (Tasks do not have this chain; an earlier plan draft named tasks alongside projects/clients -- verified against the current cli/src/commands/*.ts and corrected here.)

entries.operationOrFamily: name-for-id resolver family (every tool accepting a name in an id slot)
entries.reason: When a resolver name-to-id lookup is ambiguous or unknown, the MCP surface returns a grounded clarification receipt (real candidate ids, a question, and it never reaches the write or list API) instead of guessing or failing opaquely. SDK and CLI resolvers do not have this stop -- they either resolve deterministically or throw.

entries.operationOrFamily: risky write tools (business writes, external side effects, privileged writes, destructive writes)
entries.reason: Every MCP tool whose confirmation metadata is preview_token requires a dry_run call first, returning a confirm_token bound to a hash of the preview and the business args; the real write is refused without a matching, unexpired, unused token. SDK and CLI writes execute directly with no preview/confirm handshake.

entries.operationOrFamily: discriminator/branch consolidation: one MCP tool covers several near-identical SDK operations behind a single enum arg or an optional arg's presence/absence
entries.reason: rateKind on clockify_tasks_set_rate / clockify_projects_set_member_rate / clockify_users_set_member_rate picks between the SDK's separate cost-rate and hourly/billable-rate update operations with one discriminator arg instead of two near-identical tools. changeType+types on clockify_entity_changes_list route the single changeType-routed feed to whichever of getCreatedEntityInfo/getDeletedEntityInfo/getUpdatedEntityInfo the caller means (already the getUpdatedEntityInfo override's own recorded reason in docs/operation-parity-overrides.json). type on clockify_approvals_submit_with_type and statusType on clockify_time_off_requests_update_status are the same one-tool-many-actions shape (tool names literally say 'with_type'/'update_status'). clockify_scheduling_assignments_list_per_project branches on projectId's presence between the single-project GET (.../projects/totals/{projectId}) and the all-projects search, which carries its own page/pageSize pagination on the all-projects branch.

Less-common request-body fields for the 4 report-generation tools and 2 scheduling tools are grouped under one validated, optional, described `extra` object param (commonReportExtraSchema / attendanceReportExtraSchema / expenseReportExtraSchema / schedulingPublishExtraSchema / schedulingCapacityExtraSchema) instead of flattening dozens of secondary fields as top-level MCP args, keeping the common-case tool schema small. generateDetailedReportV1 (the expense detailed report) was mis-mapped to clockify_expenses_list before this item's operation-parity-overrides.json fix landed it on the correct clockify_reports_expense tool, where it fits this same family.

entries.operationOrFamily: nested request-body sub-object flattened into top-level args, with user/group name-or-id lists resolved before reassembly
entries.reason: Holiday/time-off-policy tools flatten a nested body sub-object (datePeriod: {startDate, endDate}, approve: {requiresApproval}) into top-level scalar args and resolve userIds/userGroupIds through resolveUserRefs/resolveGroupRefs before reassembling the nested shape for the SDK call -- verified directly in mcp/src/tools/holidays.ts (datePeriod) and mcp/src/tools/timeOff/policies.ts (approve). Time-off balance-assignment and request tools do the same for their own period sub-objects (timeOffPeriod: {isHalfDay, halfDayPeriod} verified in mcp/src/tools/timeOff/requests.ts). clockify_projects_list's clientId wraps into the SDK's array-shaped `clients` filter (verified: `req.clients = [args.clientId]`). The remaining members (updateProjectEstimate's active, createRecurringAssignment's published, updateRecurringAssignment's resolved userId/projectId, addInvoice's note/subject, invoice status filters, postWorkspacesWorkspaceIdTimeEntries's computed durationSeconds convenience field) are the same shape: a friendlier top-level arg standing in for a nested or computed body field.

entries.operationOrFamily: client-side pagination/filter controls layered onto an operation with no matching raw query params
entries.reason: clockify_expenses_list mirrors wrapper/expense-list.ts's listExpensesFiltered options (offset/limit/maxPages/start/end) exactly -- the same client-side pagination-plus-date-filter helper documented in wrapper/README.md's Expense date filtering section and demoed in docs/cookbook.md's Envelope Flattening section, since the server ignores start/end query params for this endpoint. clockify_webhooks_delivery_diagnose and clockify_audit_log_search add their own pageSize/status/authorIds/authorsMode client-facing controls the raw POST-body search endpoints do not expose as query params. getWorkspacesWorkspaceIdTimeEntriesStatusInProgress (a no-param 'list in-progress' endpoint) is wired to the general-purpose clockify_entries_list tool, which carries that tool's own start/end/description filters -- not a mis-mapping (both goMcp and tsMcp independently infer the same tool with no override), just a general list tool reused for a narrower operation.

entries.operationOrFamily: shared-reports: snake_case id alias plus a visibility toggle sourced from a nested body field
entries.reason: mcp/src/tools/sharedReports.ts declares shared_report_id (snake_case) as the arg name and maps it to the SDK's sharedReportId immediately at every call site (verified: `sharedReportId: args.shared_report_id` at 3 call sites) -- a deliberate rename, not a new capability. export_type and public are additional top-level args standing in for fields the raw create/update body nests differently.

The tool declares `body: z.never().optional()` alongside `workspaceId: z.never().optional()` -- a deliberate poisoned-name guard so a model that reflexively passes a raw `body` object (mirroring the SDK's own request shape) gets a clear validation rejection instead of the value being silently dropped or misused. Providing `body` always fails validation; it exists to be rejected, not to add capability.

entries.operationOrFamily: filterWorkspaceUsers reused as the group-membership roster lookup
entries.reason: Already curated in docs/operation-parity-overrides.json: 'The workspace user-info search endpoint is used internally to resolve group membership rosters; there is no standalone user-search tool.' groupId is the filter clockify_groups_list_members needs that the generic user-search body does not carry as a named field.
